capabilities: Wrap typed or pasted text as additions
Preserve deleted text as deletion markup
Accept or reject a change at the cursor or all changes at once
Jump to the next or previous change
Show a floating indicator with navigation and accept/reject controls
disambiguation: Not a version-history or file-diff tool; it marks edits inline in the note text.
extras: Falls back to native <ins> tags when Extended Markdown Syntax is missing; the addition syntax can be overridden in settings (Auto, Force ++...++, Force <ins>...).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to mark suggested edits inline as you write, so additions and deletions are hard to tell apart and review later.

relations.evidence: ++...++ syntax depends on Extended Markdown Syntax (extended-markdown-syntax).

summary: Track-changes mode that wraps typed text in ++addition++ markup and keeps deleted text as %%~~deletion~~%% markup while editing.
